# password-reset — spec.md

## Requirements

### Requirement: Request password reset link

ID: REQ-001
Sources: [intent]
Status: agreed

The system accepts a `POST /password-reset` request with a registered user's email address and replies with the same outward response regardless of whether the address is known.

#### Acceptance scenarios

- Given a registered email, when the operator POSTs `/password-reset`, the handler publishes `password-reset.requested` to the messaging bus and replies `202 Accepted` with body `{ "status": "queued" }`.
- Given an unknown email, when the operator POSTs `/password-reset`, the handler emits no publish, writes a counter increment to `tracing`, and replies `202 Accepted` with body `{ "status": "queued" }`.
- Given a malformed email (fails RFC-5322), when the operator POSTs `/password-reset`, the handler returns `BadRequest` with `code: "invalid_email"`.

### Requirement: Reset-link expiry

ID: REQ-002
Sources: [intent]
Status: agreed

Reset links generated by this slice expire after 30 minutes.

#### Acceptance scenarios

- Given a reset link issued at T0, when the consumer follows the link at T0 + 31 minutes, the consumer-side handler (not in this slice) returns `BadRequest` with `code: "reset_link_expired"`. This slice's responsibility is to encode the 30-minute expiry into the published event payload.

### Error conditions

| Trigger                                             | `omnia_sdk::Error`              | Code                  |
|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|-----------------------|
| Email fails RFC-5322 validation                     | `BadRequest`                    | `invalid_email`       |
| Messaging publish fails (upstream unavailable)      | `BadGateway`                    | `publish_unavailable` |
| Config key `PASSWORD_RESET_TOPIC` missing at startup | `ServerError` (from `Provider::new`) | `missing_config`      |
